urls.description: Drex Router picks a model and reasoning effort for each agent turn in about 57 to 87 ms. Call the selected model with your existing keys and gateway.
urls.title: Drex Router: per-turn model routing for agents

data.text:
Qwen, GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek. And whatever launches next.

Give Drex Router a model's price, context window, and capabilities. It can evaluate new models without retraining.

Your stack keeps evolving. Your routing adapts.

Build: https://t.co/7LyFNi9uTB

Every routing decision comes with a reason.

Drex Router returns its selected model, probabilities for every candidate, and an explanation.

You control the balance between quality and cost. Your application controls the actual LLM calls. https://t.co/Y49zTAPWJ0

Not every request needs another LLM call.

Some tasks belong with frontier models. Others with smaller models, apps, or human teams.

A support request might need an answer, an action, or escalation.

Routing should depend on the work, not a fixed rule. https://t.co/WC3Qlx3h19

We tested whether better routing could reduce costs without sacrificing answer quality.

Across 306 evaluation prompts:

> Drex Router: 8.80/10 at $0.28 per 1,000 prompts.
> Jev Router: 8.84/10 at $7.80.

Same answer quality at 28x lower cost. https://t.co/8U4J60Vxvo

urls.description: Use Drex as the judge model of Oh My Pi, the terminal coding agent, for its typed decisions and the judge() helper in its eval tool.
urls.title: Oh My Pi | Nace Docs

data.text:
Try it:
1. Install omp (v18.20.0 or later)
2. /login nace
3. Set judge to nace/drex-max-v1.1 in your config

Guide: https://t.co/A7HaE09D7J
Your chat model stays the same. Drex only takes the judge role, and it returns calibrated probabilities. With Drex Max, it can read screenshots too.
